blocks.content: RUN executes a command during the build, and whatever it changes on the filesystem becomes a new layer in the image.

RUN is how a Dockerfile actually does things: install packages, compile code, create directories. Every RUN instruction executes once, while the image is being built, and its filesystem changes are captured as a new layer.

blocks.alt: A command runs, its changes become a layer

blocks.content:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
RUN npm install
RUN mkdir -p /app/logs

code.content:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
RUN npm install
RUN mkdir -p /app/logs

codes.dockerfile:
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl
RUN npm install
RUN mkdir -p /app/logs

blocks.content: 2. Not the Same as What Happens at Container Start
blocks.text: 2. Not the Same as What Happens at Container Start

blocks.content: It is easy to conflate this with CMD, but they are opposites in timing: RUN happens once, permanently, while the image is being assembled. It never runs again when a container actually starts, that is CMD's job, covered next.

blocks.alt: Build time only, never again at container start

blocks.content: 3. Chaining Commands to Avoid Extra Layers
blocks.text: 3. Chaining Commands to Avoid Extra Layers

blocks.content: Each separate RUN instruction creates its own layer, so a common practice chains related commands together with && into a single RUN line, producing one combined layer instead of several small ones, which keeps the final image leaner.

blocks.alt: Chained commands produce one layer instead of many

blocks.content:
# Several layers, more image bloat
RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get install -y curl
RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# One layer, cleaner
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

code.content:
# Several layers, more image bloat
RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get install -y curl
RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# One layer, cleaner
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

codes.dockerfile:
# Several layers, more image bloat
RUN apt-get update
RUN apt-get install -y curl
RUN rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# One layer, cleaner
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y curl && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: RUN executes a command during the build and captures its filesystem changes as a new, permanent image layer.
Chaining related commands into one RUN line with && avoids creating extra layers for what is really one logical step.
